query: Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloys have reported densities of 1.46–6 g/cm3 and commonly contain solid solutions together with intermetallic compounds. Earlier induction-melted Al–Mg-rich alloys established this structural complexity but did not resolve subsequent transformation pathways. Compositionally graded MgAlCuZnGd alloys showed region-dependent compression and corrosion performance, while studies of AlMgₓTiSnZn alloys associated Mg content with phase stability and multiple functional properties. Most prior work emphasized hardness and room-temperature compression, leaving corrosion, high-temperature oxidation, and evolution from metastable states comparatively underexplored. Within the design constraint of density below 6 g/cm3 and the tendency for constituent-property differences to promote stable intermetallic compounds, what single testable mechanistic hypothesis could explain how a non-equilibrium Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloy evolves and why that evolution changes its corrosion and high-temperature oxidation behavior? Specify an unnamed controlled comparison, predictions relative to the initial baseline, boundary conditions, supporting prior observations, and an outcome that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.intervention: Thermomechanical processing via hot rolling with a reduction ratio of 50% and subsequent annealing at 500°C for 2 hours, with optimized hot rolling and annealing parameters
generation.conditions: Hot-rolled and annealed state, followed by exposure to a corrosive environment and high-temperature oxidation testing
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of stable intermetallic compounds and refinement of grain size
generation.mechanism: Enhanced corrosion resistance and reduced high-temperature oxidation rates resulting from the formation of stable intermetallic compounds and refined grain size
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved corrosion resistance and reduced high-temperature oxidation rates due to the formation of a protective oxide layer and stable intermetallic compounds, relative to the initial baseline of as-cast alloys
generation.uncertainty: The optimization of hot rolling and annealing parameters may require further experimentation to ensure effective refinement of grain size and formation of stable intermetallic compounds.

falsification_experiment.design: Comparison of corrosion resistance and high-temperature oxidation rates between hot-rolled and annealed AlMgₓTiSnZn high-entropy alloy and as-cast alloy
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the hot-rolled and annealed alloy does not show improved corrosion resistance and reduced high-temperature oxidation rates compared to the as-cast alloy, the hypothesis is falsified.
